Predict the full area-time surface from a fit

Source: R/predict.R
predict.stareal_fit.Rd

Reconstructs the latent prevalence surface for every area and time step, in percent (as all prevalences in stareal are), observed or not, once per posterior draw. It does this by conditional simulation (Matheron's rule), which is exact given each draw. It then summarises the draws per area and time step. Each grouping in groups is aggregated draw by draw, as a weighted mean of its areas' prevalence, and then summarised. Its uncertainty therefore accounts for the correlation between areas.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'stareal_fit'
predict(
  object,
  groups = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
  exceedance = NULL,
  keep_draws = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  n_cores = NULL,
  blas_threads = 1,
  block_bytes = 5e+08,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fit_areal() object.

groups

Names of groupings of the frame (see areal_frame()) to aggregate to. Areas are always summarised.

weights

Weights of the areas in group aggregates, for example population or number of infections. The aggregate of a group is \(\sum_a w_{at} p_{at} / \sum_a w_{at}\) for each draw. Give one of: NULL (equal weights); a vector with one value per area (named by area id, or in frame order); an areas x time steps matrix (rows named by area id or in frame order; columns named by time label or in order); or a data frame with columns id, weight and optionally time (label) or t (step number), with every area-time combination present once.

n_draws

Number of posterior draws to use, taken evenly from the stored draws of all chains. NULL: all of them.

probs

Quantiles to report.

exceedance

Prevalence thresholds, in percent (e.g. 5 for 5%); for each, the posterior probability that prevalence exceeds it is reported, in a column p_gt_<threshold> (e.g. p_gt_5).

keep_draws

Ids of areas whose prevalence draws are returned in full.

seed

Random seed, a whole number. Each draw gets its own seed, drawn from this one. The caller's random-number stream is left untouched.

n_cores

Number of worker processes. Default: 1 (this session) if the whole surface fits in one block of block_bytes, otherwise the cores less one. Every worker holds its own copy of the frame's eigenvectors (8 m^2 bytes).

blas_threads

BLAS threads per worker.

block_bytes

Approximate memory for one block's draws (bytes). Areas are processed in blocks of at most this size (up to n_cores at once, each also needing about half as much again per exceedance threshold). Each block regenerates every draw's noise, so fewer, larger blocks are faster.

verbose

Report progress: the draws conditioned and predicted so far, with an estimate of the time left.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class stareal_pred:

area

one row per area and time step, in the order of area, then time step: id, the frame's groupings, t, time, date (start of the step; calendar time frames), the pooled data y and k (0 where there are none), then mean, sd and one column per quantile (q2.5, q50, ...) of prevalence, in percent (0 to 100), and one column per threshold (p_gt_5, ...), the probability (0 to 1) that prevalence exceeds it

groups

a list with one table per grouping in groups: id (the group), t, time, date and the same statistics, ordered by group, then time step

draws

if keep_draws: prevalence draws, in percent, an array (area x time step x draw)

frame, time, settings

for plotting and the record (the frame without its eigenvectors)

as.data.frame() gives the area table (or a group's, with group =); sf::st_as_sf(pr, time = ...) gives it as polygons for one time step.

Details

The surface is the field plus fixed effects, without the cell-level nugget: it is the prevalence of the area-time cell, not of one survey in it. At observed cells it therefore differs from the latent values that diagnose() and crossval() report, which include the nugget.

Examples

fr <- areal_lattice(4, 4, blocks = c(2, 2))
tf <- time_frame(n_steps = 5)
sim <- simulate_areal(fr, tf, n_cells = 30, seed = 1)
fit <- fit_areal(sim, control = list(n_iter = 100, n_burn = 50, n_store = 25, n_chains = 1,
                                     ess_sweeps = 2, verbose = FALSE))
pr <- predict(fit, groups = "block", verbose = FALSE)
head(pr$area)
